flag: none; Job A only via the hash-pinned approved list (not in approved.json until Peace posts /approve-rule on its proposal issue)
engine: a new string-parser search (peaceai/lib/derive-string.ts) reached through the same rule kind in peaceai/lib/learned-derive.ts, bound to DERIVE_STRING_TRIGGER with the params dsl typed-dsl-v5-strings and placement new-or-existing-module-v5 (all three or derive_params). It enumerates one-expression parsers of a string line (and at most one more string or number parameter q): a piece of the line (the line, a field split on one single-character delimiter with a default when the field is missing, the fields from i on joined back, the part after the last delimiter, the line with a constant or q prefix or suffix stripped), optionally trimmed before or after; returned as a string, a field count, an integer read with a fixed /^-?\d{1,12}$/ test and a default, a boolean test (=== / startsWith / endsWith / includes against a literal from the examples or q, optionally negated), or a string[] (split, optionally trimmed and with empty items dropped). It keeps every program that fits all examples (a test true on every example stays a rival), refuses when two fits disagree on any probe (the asked rows go in the detail, each chosen to tell the most rival behaviors apart), refuses an unpinned default or constant as an asked row (path gate), and re-checks the emitted text by decompiling and recompiling it. Literals holding a space are read from the raw issue text, cross-checked line by line against the cleaned text (derive_examples_raw otherwise). Job B (test-candidates.ts) re-checks a derive candidate by its own operation id: a v5 candidate only through deriveModuleRecheck / deriveAppendRecheck with the v5 checks, a v4 candidate with the v4 checks, a v1-v3 candidate exactly as before
scope: an issue whose header reads 'Add a new module src/....ts exporting the string parser NAME(line: string[, q: string|number]): string|number|boolean|string[]' or 'Append a new string parser NAME(...): R to the existing module src/....ts', with literal examples (printable ASCII, no double quote or backslash, at most 120 characters); no regex built from input, no loops, no side effects, imports never added or changed
refusals: derive_examples (count, arity, types, length, contradiction, characters); derive_examples_raw (a literal with a space read only from cleaned text, or a raw Examples list that differs from the cleaned one, hides lines in a comment or a fence, or lexes differently); derive_signature; derive_under_specified_outputs / _unread / _path (asked row); derive_no_fit; derive_ambiguous (asked rows in the detail); derive_budget (more than 20000 fits or probes); derive_string_expr; derive_params; every v1 new-module path refusal and every v3 append refusal; new_test_path_exists; denied_path. Escaping (replace chains such as escapeCheckinNote) is out of scope and refused; it is recorded as v6 scope

evidence.method: new upstream evidence for one-expression string functions (GitHub code search, MIT / Apache-2.0 only), each re-derived from a seeded grid slice plus only the rows its refusals asked for (answered by the upstream function) and checked against the upstream function on every held-out grid row and 400 probe rows
evidence.note: Entries marked outOfVocabulary are kept on purpose to show the limit below. See peaceai/docs/m114-string-parsing.md.

limits: Known limit (disclosed): when the true function is outside v5's vocabulary (trimStart before a two-character prefix, `.pop() || path`, `split()[1] || default`, a fixed slice, escaping), the examples can be fitted by an in-vocabulary program that is wrong elsewhere; 3 of the 4 out-of-vocabulary evidence entries show this. The probes carry no expected outputs, so nothing checks the program against the true function beyond the examples and asked rows. The claim is only that no in-vocabulary rival fit was missed: every program in the vocabulary that fits the examples is compared on the probes, and any two that disagree are refused. Other limits: single-character delimiters only; no escapes, newlines or tabs inside literals; non-integer q values are not probed; large searches refuse with derive_budget; tests on q (hasTag) can need many asked rows. Credit still rests on Peace's verdict on each real candidate.
